Proof 1: LLN: sample mean of i.i.d. RVs with finite mean converges to E[X]

Statement: LLN: sample mean of i.i.d. RVs with finite mean converges to E[X]

Hypotheses: X_1,...,X_n i.i.d., E[X_1] = mu exists

Conclusion: X_bar_n -> mu as n -> infinity (a.s.)

Definitions: LLN, i.i.d., sample mean, convergence

Proof (Variation #1):

Step 1: X_bar = (1/n) sum X_i

Step 2: Var(X_bar) = sigma^2/n -> 0

Step 3: By Chebyshev: P(|X_bar - mu| > eps) <= sigma^2/(n*eps^2) -> 0

Step 4: Strong LLN: use Kolmogorov criterion or Borel-Cantelli

ID: b581de8af84a | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n)

Mutation test: Removing 'i.i.d.': dependent variables can violate LLN

Provenance: Variation #1 for theorem in domain Probability

Proof 2: CLT: normalized sum of i.i.d. RVs converges to N(0,1)

Statement: CLT: normalized sum of i.i.d. RVs converges to N(0,1)

Hypotheses: X_i i.i.d., E[X_i]=0, Var(X_i)=1

Conclusion: S_n/sqrt(n) converges to N(0,1) in distribution

Definitions: CLT, normal distribution, convergence in distribution

Proof (Variation #2):

Step 1: Compute characteristic function phi(t) of X_1

Step 2: Taylor expand: phi(t) = 1 - t^2/2 + o(t^2)

Step 3: Char func of S_n/sqrt(n) is [phi(t/sqrt(n))]^n

Step 4: = [1 - t^2/(2n) + o(1/n)]^n -> exp(-t^2/2)

Step 5: Levy continuity theorem: convergence of char funcs implies convergence in distribution

ID: bc7bfd1bff6f | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^2)

Mutation test: Removing 'Var=1' (finite variance): Cauchy distribution fails CLT

Provenance: Variation #2 for theorem in domain Probability

Proof 3: Markov inequality: P(X >= a) <= E[X]/a for X >= 0

Statement: Markov inequality: P(X >= a) <= E[X]/a for X >= 0

Hypotheses: X >= 0 a.s., a > 0, E[X] finite

Conclusion: P(X >= a) <= E[X]/a

Definitions: Markov, inequality, nonnegative

Proof (Variation #3):

Step 1: E[X] = E[X * 1_{X>=a}] + E[X * 1_{X

Step 2: >= E[X * 1_{X>=a}] >= a * P(X >= a)

Step 3: Divide by a: E[X]/a >= P(X >= a)

Step 4: Conclude by logical deduction from Step 3
